subject: science
passage: When a honeybee colony outgrows its hive, thousands of bees leave with the old queen and cluster on a branch while scouts search for a new home. Returning scouts perform waggle dances advertising the sites they have found, and bees that have inspected a better site dance for it longer. Over several days, dances for inferior sites die out. Biologist Rafael Moreno argues that the swarm reaches its decision when the dancers achieve consensus, all advertising the same site, at which point the swarm takes flight.
passage_b: The dances clearly do the work of comparing sites: better sites recruit more inspectors. But the trigger for departure lies elsewhere. Scouts visiting a candidate site keep track, apparently by how often they encounter one another, of how many bees are present there. Once that number passes a threshold, they return and begin preparing the swarm to fly, sometimes while dances for rival sites are still under way. The choice is settled by a quorum at the site, not by unanimity on the cluster.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the account of how the swarm reaches its decision in Text 1?

choices.A: By rejecting the idea that waggle dances help the swarm compare possible nest sites
choices.B: By arguing that a swarm departs only after every scout has inspected the chosen site
choices.C: By claiming that dances for inferior sites always continue until the swarm takes flight
choices.D: By agreeing that dances compare sites but locating the decision in a quorum at the site

explanation.why: Text 2 agrees that "The dances clearly do the work of comparing sites." But it says departure is triggered when the number of scouts at one site "passes a threshold," "sometimes while dances for rival sites are still under way." So the decision comes from a quorum at the site, not the consensus among dancers that Moreno describes.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says the dances "clearly do the work of comparing sites."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says a threshold number of bees at the site is enough; it never requires every scout to visit.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says rival dances continue only "sometimes"; it does not say they always last until departure.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 keeps the dances' role in comparing sites but argues that a quorum of scouts at a site, not unanimous dancing, settles the choice.
